pages.title: Neal Bushaw
pages.description: Neal Bushaw, Associate Professor of Mathematics at Virginia Commonwealth University: combinatorics, graph theory, publications, teaching.

sections.heading: Research

publicationTopics.label: Extremal problems for graphs
publicationTopics.description: Forbidden configurations, saturation, intersection problems, and structural graph theory.

publicationTopics.label: Extremal problems for hypergraphs
publicationTopics.description: Turán-type and saturation questions for hypergraphs and Berge configurations.

publicationTopics.label: Additive number theory
publicationTopics.description: Zero-sum, sum-free, and related problems in finite abelian groups.

publicationTopics.label: Automated conjecturing
publicationTopics.description: Using computation to discover mathematical patterns, formulate conjectures, and support teaching.

publicationTopics.label: Mathematical music theory
publicationTopics.description: Discrete models of rhythm, tuning, balance, and maximal evenness.

publicationTopics.label: Bootstrap percolation
publicationTopics.description: Percolation thresholds and contagious processes on grids, tilings, and graphs.

publicationTopics.label: Probability and random processes
publicationTopics.description: Threshold phenomena, stochastic processes, and probabilistic methods.

publicationTopics.label: Graph invariants and optimization
publicationTopics.description: Extremal values of graph parameters, vertex configurations, and colorings.

sections.talksNote: In August 2022 this was declared a “highlights” section, and is no longer guaranteed to be exhaustive. There are talks which are lost to the sands of time — if you have a hint of a memory of a vision of seeing me give a talk somewhere and it isn't in this list, it is best to assume it probably happened. Or you could invite me for a repeat.
